rules.name: Breadth Requirement
rules.desc:
Remaining units for the minor must be completed by taking at least one course across each of three streams below:

• Foundations: courses that explore the fundamental theoretical or historical foundations of human rights

• Contemporary Issues: courses that offer a depth of study on a particular human rights issue, or the human rights reality of a specific geography, social group, or context

• Practice: courses dedicated to the practical application of human rights principles through skills development, advocacy training, and experiential or community-engaged learning
To discuss courses and course plan the for minor, please make an appointment with our Student Services Specialist.

rules.name: Capstone
rules.desc:
To fulfill the Capstone requirement, students may choose between one of two pathways: the Independent Project Pathway or the Course Equivalency Pathway.
As soon as students declare the Minor, they will be assigned an orientation module to complete in Canvas, including a required brainstorm form and advising session. Following these steps, students must complete and submit their capstone proposals by Week 7 of the quarter before their intended capstone term.
Upon completion of the capstone, students must submit their work for archiving in the Stanford Digital Repository.
rules.notes:
1. Independent Project Pathway
• Under the supervision of an approved faculty member, students propose and complete a 3-5 unit capstone project that should either include:
- a 25-page research paper on a human rights topic approved by the supervising faculty; or
- an alternative culminating work requiring equivalent effort, such as an original short film produced by the student, an annotated digital human rights database, a curated exhibit, or a software application designed to address human rights challenges, approved in advance by the supervising faculty.
• Student choosing this option will enroll in HUMRTS 199 to complete a self-designed capstone deliverable by agreed-upon deadlines
• Final capstone is to be graded by the faculty advisor
2. Course Equivalency Pathway
• Submit a proposal to use work you will complete in an existing 3-5 unit course to fulfill the capstone requirement
• Students choosing this option will enroll in an existing course and complete assignments and final projects that will serve as a capstone deliverable
• Final capstone grade is to be assigned by the course instructor

rules.name: GPA of 3.0 or higher in the minor's courses
At least 10 of the 25 units on Stanford's campus

gpa: All students must maintain a GPA of no less than 3.0 in the classes counting toward the minor.
grading: All courses counted toward the minor must be taken for a letter grade, except where letter grades are not offered, as university policy requires.
policies:
• Completion of a minimum of 25 units of Human Rights related coursework.

• Students may not double-count courses to complete major and minor requirements.

• At least 10 of the 25 units must be completed on Stanford’s campus.

• To ensure timely completion, students shall declare the Minor in Human Rights no later than 2 quarters before degree conferral. Special cases or exceptions must be discussed with our Student Services Specialist and are subject to program approval
transferPolicy: Transfer credits accepted by the university Registrar as counting toward graduation requirements are eligible to be petitioned for credit within the Human Rights minor.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 25 units: HUMRTS 101, at least one course from each of the Foundations, Contemporary Issues and Practice lists (more courses from these lists fill the remaining units), and a 3-5 unit capstone by proposal, all letter graded where a letter grade is offered. These courses cannot also count toward your major. Checked by hand: the capstone pathway, the 3.0 GPA in the minor's courses, at least 10 units on Stanford's campus, and petitioned transfer credit. Declare the minor at least two quarters before your degree is conferred.
